title: Console MVP: slice and unify insight card flow to reduce cost/tracing surface
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Decision ticket to narrow Console insight cards and unify the card rendering/workflow so we can ship a compact MVP surface that limits trace sampling and cost attribution volume. This ticket scopes explicit cuts, lists acceptance criteria for shipping an operable MVP, and documents the engineering/UX trade-offs for later re-expansion.
background: Multiple PMs and Design reviews flagged that the initial Insights card set introduces high cardinality traces and large cost delta computations which push telemetry and query costs above the 2025-Q1 budget. The engineering team has limited cycles to implement full-featured tracing and route cost breakdowns before the planned alpha. We need surgical reductions that preserve core value: per-route latency, token-cost attribution, and error surface for quick troubleshooting.
proposed_scope_cut: 1) Collapse card variants: replace 6 card types with 3 compact cards (route health, cost-snapshot, top-errors). 2) Disable per-token breakdown in launch; show aggregated token buckets (prompt, completion, embeddings) instead. 3) Default trace sampling to 1% for all non-enterprise accounts and 5% for Dedicated trials. 4) Defer drill-down tracing (deep spans) behind the 'advanced telemetry' opt-in. 5) Remove live-streamed token-level cost graphs from MVP and instead expose nightly aggregated CSV export.
tradeoffs: - UX: Users lose immediate per-token granularity which sacrifices some debugging speed. - Engineering: Simpler telemetry pipeline reduces SLO risk but requires later migrations for higher fidelity. - Cost: Cuts reduce ingestion and storage by estimated 45% in alpha workloads. - Future work: Restoring per-token breakdown will require added KV cache instrumentation and indexed storage which is scoped for post-MVP work.
open_questions: What is the exact threshold for enterprise accounts to get higher trace sampling? (ops or contract-based?)
Should the compact cards be horizontally scrollable on mobile or stacked? (Design prefers stacked, Eng prefers scroll)
Do we expose sampling toggle in the Console or keep it controlled server-side until GA?
acceptance_criteria: Compact card set (route health, cost-snapshot, top-errors) displays in Console for all users without layout regressions on desktop and mobile.
Per-route cost shown as aggregated buckets (prompt/completion/embeddings) and matches nightly CSV totals within 2% for alpha traffic patterns.
Trace ingestion reduced to targeted sampling rates (1% default, 5% Dedicated trial) and verified by telemetry dashboard during smoke tests.
Deep-span drilldown UI hidden behind 'advanced telemetry' flag; toggling false returns no deep-span panels and prevents extra trace ingestion.
Nightly CSV export job runs and is accessible for alpha customers; CSV schema documented in linked Confluence page.
Rollout plan documented and gated by performance smoke test (pass/fail) and on-call playbook updated for trace anomalies.
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal alpha with 3 existing customers (<=10k requests/day) and staged 10%->40%->100% within 48h windows. Phase B: Open beta to all self-serve accounts with sampling limits enforced. Disable by default for enterprise until contract amendment. Monitor cost deltas and errors for 7 days before GA. Abort criteria: >5% increase in request error surface or >10% discrepancy in cost attribution vs. billing projections.
updates: 2025-02-11: Ticket created after cross-functional tradeoff workshop. Initial cuts proposed by PM to meet alpha cost target.
2025-02-12: Eng feasibility check: suggested deferring per-token breakdown and exposing aggregated buckets; estimated 5 points for implementation and rollout gating.
2025-02-13: Design uploaded compact card mocks; recommended stacked layout for mobile to reduce complexity. Linked in artifacts.
2025-02-14: SRE requested explicit abort criteria and a runbook entry — added to acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
2025-02-16: Security review triage concluded no new data retention risk for aggregated buckets; advanced telemetry opt-in flagged for later DSR and retention review.
2025-02-18: PM review meeting — agreed on default sampling rates and CSV export for alpha. Ready for Eng PR and design handoff.

Asha Menon (Design): Compact cards trade usability for performance; recommend a short tooltip that explains missing per-token detail in MVP.
Marta Kuznetsova (Infra): We estimate ~48h of infra time to add sampling enforcement and staging flags; recommend feature-flag rollout.
Theo Brooks (SRE): Add a Grafana alert for unexpected spike in trace volume after rollout to trigger immediate rollback.
